Countdown.dc.html.title: Counting down to the next event

howto.text: Laptop-landscape (1366x768), not a phone layout - this runs on the deployed laptop, chrome-free (sidebar/nav already hidden by showSidebar). Three states: counting down to a scheduled event, nothing scheduled at all, and the exit dialog. The real scanner UI already exists and isn't redesigned here - this screen only covers the moment before it.

design.text:
WHY IT LOOKS LIKE THIS

Four big tiles for the countdown, not a sentence of text - readable from across the room, which a kiosk needs to be. Each unit is labelled (HOURS/MINUTES/SECONDS) so the numbers are never ambiguous at a glance.

The top bar is the only chrome this screen has - org name + a pulsing 'Listening' dot + a live clock, so a passerby can tell at a glance the system is alive and not frozen, without any navigation inviting them to tap around.

Exit kiosk is a quiet corner link, not a button - it should never be the most visually prominent thing on the screen. It opens the real AlertDialog.Content (corner X included, same primitive fixed earlier this session) requiring the account password - no shortcut around that.

nothingNote.text: Deliberately a different message, not the countdown screen with zeroes in it - 'Nothing scheduled right now' plus a line confirming the kiosk is still watching and will update on its own. A countdown showing 00:00:00 would read as broken; this reads as calm and correct.

exitNote.text: The kiosk screen dims behind the dialog rather than navigating away first - makes clear this is a confirmation ON the kiosk, not a different screen or a route change. Cancel returns straight to the live countdown/scanner with nothing changed.
